title: Frozen-physics numerical implementation and integrator viability
central_question: Can the frozen S4/G8 reduced equations be integrated robustly and at materially lower computational cost than the current Python iterative-Heun route, without changing representation, closure or forcing?

prospective_gates.robustness: All 8 purpose/material cases complete with finite state, qualified constitutive domain and water-ledger <=1e-8 cm.
prospective_gates.numerical_refinement: RK4_FIXED vs RK4_HALF purpose metrics remain small relative to RK4_FIXED vs R128 hydrological error; report componentwise, no scalar gate.
prospective_gates.performance: Same-job compiled RK4_FIXED wall time is compared to R128_T32 and to Python H_FIXED where H_FIXED completes.
prospective_gates.practical_speed_support: RK4_FIXED/R128 wall ratio <1 for every completed validation case and no robustness failure.
prospective_gates.no_speed_support: Any validation RK4_FIXED/R128 wall ratio >=1, or compiled candidate fails robustness.

attribution_rules: If compiled RK4 is robust where Python Heun blocks, attribute the P3 blocking primarily to the iterative-Heun numerical policy/implementation, not to frozen G8 physics.
If compiled RK4 also blocks in the same cases, retain a frozen-equation numerical stiffness/robustness limitation.
If compiled RK4 is faster than R128 while preserving the P3 error regime, implementation overhead explained the P3 speed reversal.
If compiled RK4 remains slower than R128, state-count reduction is not sufficient for practical speed under this workload.
